doc.title: Jack Sheldon interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 15, 1999

title: Working with Gene Brant's band at age 12
summary: Wartime opportunity: joined the union and played society band jobs, learned to read, and was paid like an adult.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Interesting you say that. A lot of the musicians went in the service, did that open some opportunities for a young guy like you?

Yeah it was great for me, yeah. I was young and I got in a union, I went down with a pipe. Gene Brant got me, and this was a great guy, a trombone player, and he worked at the George Washington Hotel, sort of a society band I guess, I really don’t remember now what it was we played. Although I don’t know, he always thought he was jazz I’m sure. And he taught me how to read. He struggled with me to teach me syncopation and get me so I could read the stuff. Then I went in and I guess I got a suit, I got a blue suit, and I went in and started playing when I was about 12, or the same year that I got the trumpet. I started working right away.
Were they paying you as a 12 year old the same money that they were giving the adults?

I think so. I never really asked. I never knew. But I think they thought I was an adult, with that suit you know. I could go up to the bar, I remember I got a whiskey sour, and it was much harder to play, after I kept seeing a lot of different clusters of notes.
But that didn’t bother me though.
